title: Enterprise Dedicated Matchmaker: SLA-to-GPU Profiling & Scaling Policy Playbook
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Problem: Sales/SEs and Customer Success frequently bring requests for dedicated GPU capacity without a clear, repeatable way to translate customer SLAs and workload patterns into a recommended reserved throughput profile, GPU family, and scaling policy. This results in ad-hoc sizing, costly overprovisioning, and back-and-forth with customers during onboarding.

Goals:
- Create a lightweight decision playbook ("Matchmaker") that maps SLA targets and workload signals to an initial reserved throughput recommendation, GPU class family, and a default scaling policy.
- Embed the Matchmaker outputs into the intake wizard used by Solutions Engineering and the Concierge team so customers get a pre-filled recommendation during intake.
- Produce an internal scoring rubric and a one-page cheat sheet for AE/SEs to defend the recommendation during negotiation.

Scope:
- In-scope: prototyping a rules-based Matchmaker, scoring rubric for SLA/throughput mapping, 3 preset scaling policy templates (latency-SLO, cost-optimized, throughput-guarantee), GPU family mapping heuristics (A100/RTX/Trenton-equivalents), integration points in intake form, handoff checklist for Dedicated onboarding.
- Out-of-scope: fully automated ML-based recommender, billing contract changes, new GPU procurement.

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Intake signals captured: expected p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec per user, concurrency profile (steady vs spiky), batchability score (high/med/low), model family and sequence length distribution, data sensitivity (affects Private vs Hosted decision).
2) Scoring rubric (weights): SLA severity (40%), concurrency shape (20%), batchability (15%), model token cost (15%), regulatory constraint (10%). Score -> profile band (Bronze/Silver/Gold/Platinum).
3) Band -> recommended reserved throughput (tokens/sec) baseline, GPU family suggestion, and scaling policy:
   - Bronze: cost-first, CPU/low-tier GPU or small A100 slice, conservative reserved throughput, autoscale off by default, burst credits allowed.
   - Silver: balanced, standard A100/80GB or RTX equivalent, autoscale with slow ramp, 2x burst tolerance.
   - Gold: performance-first for p95 latency, A100-class reserved, aggressive autoscale + KV cache tuning, pre-warm lanes.
   - Platinum: enterprise SLA (99.95+), dedicated cluster with affinity routing, multi-region fallback, guaranteed reserved throughput, tracked SLO budget.
4) Scaling policy presets: latency-SLO (prioritize p95 with reactive ramp), cost-optimized (maximize batching and KV cache, slow scale-up), throughput-guarantee (maintain steady tokens/sec with pre-provisioned slots).
5) Fallbacks & graceful degradation: automated model variant fallthrough (quantized model with slightly different quality), regional failover, quota throttling with customer-level notifications.

Deliverables:
- PM playbook doc + one-pager cheat sheet for AEs/SEs.
- Intake form changes (prefill + explanation) and prototype UI copy.
- Engineering spec for mapping logic and API surface.
- Pilot onboarding with 3 customers (one each: Bronze/Silver/Gold).

Stakeholders: SEs (Maya Chen), Concierge (Diego Alvarez), Runtime Eng (Priya Nair), Infra (Jon Keller), Legal/Contracts (Hannah Wu), Observability (Rory Patel).

Metrics of success:
- Reduce average onboarding conversation time from intake to signed reservation by 40%.
- First-pass recommendation acceptance rate >= 70% in pilot.
- Reduction in initial committed GPU oversizing (baseline measurement) by 25%.
